**West Virginia** is a location in the United States mentioned throughout the Fallout Series and is where the majority of Fallout 76 takes place. Post-war, most of what was West Virginia is often colloquially referred to as Appalachia. 

West Virginia was founded on June 20, 1863. [3] It was originally part of Virginia during the American Civil War. [4] 

- Edgar Blackburn writes in a log that he is returning to West Virginia. [5] 
- Russell Dorsey mentions the Brotherhood of Steel's plans to travel to the state. [6] 
- The seal of the state of West Virginia is seen on several signs, such as the Helvetia placard.
- The Department of the Interior West Virginia Park Service emblems are found after the war. [7] 
- Fire stations before the war utilized fire axes with the state name engraved on the top. [8] 
- On December 15, 1967, the Silver Bridge collapsed. The sign commemorating the event has a West Virginia state seal. [9] 
- The West Virginia Lottery Company game Lucky Hits! was the largest ever lottery game in the state. [10] [11] 
- Junk mail was sent to an address in Charleston, West Virginia. [12] 
- Paul encouraged his friend Gary to apply for a job at the West Virginia lumberyard, noting better pay and no automation. The address to the location is listed as State Route 81A in the town of Friendly. [13] [14] 
- The front of the Morgantown Airport reads "Welcome to Morgantown, West Virginia." [15] 
- A tourist sign displays the state's nickname, "the Mountain State." [1] 
- A note mentions that the government, the mining companies, and Vault-Tec aim to have the state run by machines. [16] 
- RobCo Industries had a West Virginia division research facility in Watoga. [17] 
- The eviction notice has addresses including the state name.
- Several Pleasant Valley Ski Resort posters feature the state name. [18] 
- Anne Litzinger shares that she wants to explore West Virginia after graduation, hoping to be a photojournalist. [19] 
- Harold Clark recorded a message, sharing that he was locked in Vault-Tec's Vault 51 in the Appalachia region of West Virginia. [20] 
- Uncanny Caverns poster features the state name. [21] 
- West Virginia was home to many varieties of sparrows, including the lark sparrow, the field sparrow, the vesper sparrow, and the fox sparrow. [22] 
- A reproduction of the Liberty Bell was presented to the state in 1950. [23] [24] 
- The name of the state is on the Crevasse Dam sign. [25] 
- In an edition of *Informant* , the state is mentioned in the subheader, "what exactly is going on in the woods of West Virginia?" [26] 
- Charleston's main city sign is labeled with the state name. [27] 
- The Pioneer Scouts of West Virginia's Camp Lewis mentions the state name. [28] [29] 
- Issue #6 of *Scouts' Life* features Pioneer Scouts West Virginia Troop 24. [30] 
- The Clarksburg city limits sign is stylized in the shape of the state. [31] 
- The Whitespring Resort has a West Virginia room. [32] 
- School buses in Appalachia read "West Virginia School District" on the side. [33] 
- Several maps of West Virginia can be found throughout the Appalachian region. [34] 
- West Virginia's naturally occurring cranberry, pitcher, and sundew plants are mentioned as existing post-War. [35] 
- A Spruce Knob sign describes the highest point in West Virginia, at 4,863 feet of elevation. [1] 
- The New Appalachian Railroad installed warning signage and poles for underground cable, noting the state in the instructions. [36] [37] 
- The state is mentioned in several Pioneer Scout exams including herpotologist, mammalogist, archaeologist, collector, and robotocist variants. [38] [39] [40] [41] [42] 
- A statue and museum featuring a local folklore legend known as the Mothman is situated in Point Pleasant, West Virginia. [43] A poster for the Mothman Museum also features the state name. [44] 
- The Miners Monument features a placard that reads "West Virginia Coal Miners." [45] 
- Both signs at Sugar Grove display the state's shape and abbreviation. [46] [47] 
- West Virginia is mentioned in the Exodus and Observations, vol. XXVII notes in *Fallout 76* , introduced in the*Night of the Moth* update.
- The West Virginia Dept of Environmental Affairs is mentioned on a sign above The Burning Mine. [48] 
- White Sulphur Springs is located in West Virginia. [49] 
- Workers in the state were reported to "refuse to take it lying down." [50] 
- The Firing Range Posters were printed in West Virginia.
- One of the state lines runs west of the Silver Bridge in Point Pleasant. [51]
